{{short description|Theorem in category theory}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Lawvere's fixed-point theorem''' is an important result in [[category theory]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Soto-Andrade |first1=Jorge |last2=J. Varela |first2=Francisco |title=Self-Reference and Fixed Points: A Discussion and an Extension of Lawvere's Theorem |journal=Acta Applicandae Mathematicae |date=1984 |volume=2 |doi=10.1007/BF01405490 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01405490|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It is a broad abstract generalization of many diagonal arguments in mathematics and logic, such as [[Cantor's diagonal argument]], [[Cantor's theorem]], [[Russell's paradox]], [[Gödel's first incompleteness theorem]], [[Turing's proof|Turing's solution to the Entscheidungsproblem]], and [[Tarski's undefinability theorem]].<ref name = "yanofsky">{{cite journal |last1=Yanofsky |first1=Noson |title=A Universal Approach to Self-Referential Paradoxes, Incompleteness and Fixed Points |journal=[[The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic]] |date=September 2003 |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=362–386 |doi=10.2178/bsl/1058448677|arxiv=math/0305282 }}</ref>

It was first proven by [[William Lawvere]] in 1969.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Lawvere |first1=Francis William |author1-link=William Lawvere |title=Category Theory, Homology Theory and their Applications II (Lecture Notes in Mathematics, vol 92) |date=1969 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/BFb0080769 |chapter=Diagonal arguments and Cartesian closed categories}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lawvere |first1=William |author1-link=William Lawvere |title=Diagonal arguments and cartesian closed categories with author commentary |journal=Reprints in Theory and Applications of Categories |date=2006 |issue=15 |pages=1–13 |url=http://tac.mta.ca/tac/reprints/articles/15/tr15abs.html}}</ref>

== Statement ==
Lawvere's theorem states that, for any [[Cartesian closed category]] <math>\mathbf{C}</math> and given an object <math>B</math> in it, if there is a [[Point-surjective morphism#Definition#Weak point-surjectivity|weakly point-surjective]] [[morphism]] <math>f</math>  from some object <math>A</math> to the [[exponential object]] <math>B^A</math>, then every [[endomorphism ]]<math>g: B \rightarrow B</math> has a fixed point. That is, there exists a morphism <math> b : 1 \rightarrow B</math> (where <math>1</math> is a [[Initial and terminal objects| terminal object]] in <math>\mathbf{C}</math> ) such that <math>g \circ b = b</math>.

This can be further generalized to a much broader class of categories. Let <math>\mathbf{C}</math> be a category equipped with a [[functor]] <math>\sharp : \mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{C} \rightarrow \mathbf{C}</math>, a chosen object <math>t</math>, and [[natural transformation]] <math>\delta : id_\mathbf{C} \Rightarrow \sharp \circ \Delta_C</math>. Let <math>F : A \sharp A \rightarrow C</math> and <math>\sigma : C \rightarrow C</math> be morphisms in <math>\mathbf{C}</math> such that, <math>\exists a_0 : t \rightarrow A, \forall a : t \rightarrow A</math>, such that <math>\sigma \circ F \circ \delta_A \circ a = F \circ (a_0 \sharp a) \circ \delta_t</math>. Then the map <math>c := F \circ \delta \circ a_0 : t \rightarrow C</math> satisfies <math>\sigma \circ c = c</math>. <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Roberts |first=David Michael |date=2023-08-10 |title=Substructural fixed-point theorems and the diagonal argument: theme and variations |url=https://compositionality.episciences.org/13527 |journal=Compositionality |language=en |volume=5 |doi=10.32408/compositionality-5-8 |issn=2631-4444|arxiv=2110.00239 }}</ref>

==Applications==

The theorem's [[contrapositive]] is particularly useful in proving many results. It states that if there is an object <math>B</math> in the category such that there is an endomorphism <math>g: B \rightarrow B</math> that has no fixed points, then there is no object <math>A</math> with a weakly point-surjective map <math>f : A \rightarrow B^A </math>. Some important corollaries of this are:<ref name="yanofsky" /> 
* [[Cantor's theorem]]
* [[Cantor's diagonal argument]]
* [[Diagonal lemma]]
* [[Russell's paradox]]
* [[Gödel's first incompleteness theorem]]
* [[Tarski's undefinability theorem]]
* [[Turing's proof]]
* [[Löb's paradox]]
* [[Kleene's recursion theorem#Rogers's fixed-point theorem|Roger's fixed-point theorem]]
* [[Rice's theorem]]
